question: A condition affects 10 of 100 people. A test catches 8 of those 10 and falsely flags 9 of the other 90. Use a 2 by 2 count grid to explain the chance a positive person has the condition.

acts.beat: Organize the 100 people by condition status.
Fill the grid with true and false test results.
Compare the positive counts to find the conditional chance.

panels.title: Start with everyone
panels.question: How many people have the condition?
panels.new_idea: Separate the 100 people into 10 affected and 90 unaffected.
panels.caption: Out of 100 people, 10 have the condition and 90 do not.

panels.title: Fill the count grid
panels.question: What happens to each group?
panels.new_idea: Place 8 true positives, 2 missed cases, 9 false positives, and 81 true negatives.
panels.caption: The test creates 8 true positives and 9 false positives.

panels.title: Look only at positives
panels.question: Who is included after a positive result?
panels.new_idea: Highlight the positive-result row containing 8 people with the condition and 9 without it.
panels.caption: A positive result includes 8 affected people and 9 unaffected people.

panels.title: Calculate the chance
panels.question: What fraction of positive people have the condition?
panels.new_idea: Use 8 favorable cases among 17 total positive results.
panels.caption: Therefore, the chance is 8 out of 17, about 47%.

takeaway: Among people who test positive, 8 of 17 have the condition, about 47%; this is not 80% because false positives add 9 unaffected people.
